label: copy-phase echo of l at original position 2-3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input is the letter l. In-copy l holds 99.5% of the activation mass, and the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Position strongly gates it. It is strongest when the echoed l was original token 2 or 3 (recall_idx 3-4: precision about 0.8, 86% of mass, and top activations around 3.0 such as "a 2 l 0 p t <DEL> a 2 [l]"). It is weak or absent when l was original token 0-1 or 4+ (recall_idx 2: 20% fire rate; recall_idx 5: 35%; recall_idx 6+: under 5%). It also tends to be off on the final output step. It does not respond to l in the original phase, other letters, the output token, or digit count. Only about 36% of all copy-phase l inputs fire.

issues: Checked and confirmed: on dev, the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases (0 of 3.73M steps; copy phase has 100% of the mass). in_tok = l carries 99.5% of the mass, and the 12 top activations (about 3.0) are all l at recall_idx 3-4. Test scores match the reported ones: P 0.811, R 0.728, F1 0.767, mass recall 0.863. The plain l-in-copy predicate gets F1 0.523 and mass recall 0.994 on test.

'Off on the final output step' overstates it. Within the recall_idx 3-4 window, the fire rate at to_go = 0 is about 0.47-0.51, versus 0.82-0.94 at to_go >= 1 (dev). The feature is weaker there, not off. Adding to_go > 0 raises precision to 0.877 but lowers test F1 to 0.749.

The recall_idx 2 miss is not uniform, so 'fire rate 20% at recall_idx 2' hides structure. The rate is 0.56 at to_go = 1 and 0.37 at to_go = 2 (short sequences), and falls to 0.02-0.05 at to_go >= 4. recall_idx 5 fires at 0.28-0.40 at every to_go. This is a small systematic miss class: an l echoed from position 1 near the end of a short sequence.

'Does not respond to digit count' is slightly off. Within the window, precision is 0.83 with n_digits = 0 versus 0.93 with n_digits >= 2, and 0.925 when the previous input is a digit versus 0.864 when it is a letter. Repeated l (in_count > 1) gives 0.81 versus 0.89. These are modest modulations, not a counterexample class.

The test misses list shows no systematic token or history class outside of l. The missed activations are low-magnitude l echoes at recall_idx 1-2 or 5+, and the false positives are mostly last-step or short-sequence l. Adding the recall_idx 2 / to_go 1 case gives test F1 0.780 (P 0.792, R 0.769, mass recall 0.892), only a small gain. The residual looks like graded position tuning, not a missing concept.
